events.summary: ZBCN holder methodology change on the 2026-10-28 regeneration: staked ZBCN is now credited to the stakers' own wallets inside Retail instead of sitting in vault custody (PR #54, the TEL way), and the CEX list grew from 46 to 51 wallets (PRs #50-#52). About 3,241 staker wallets newly appear as holders (retail holder count 111,530 to 114,763) and roughly 4.75B staked ZBCN moves from vault custody into Retail, partly offset by roughly 2.7-3.0B moving from Retail to CEX.

events.summary: Supply Breakdown now shows one top-level bucket, Developer holdings, for every project. It holds the developer-controlled categories as sub-categories (TEL: treasury, council, Telcoin Holdings, team / reward contracts, escrow; ZBCN: treasury and buyback vaults, team and allocation wallets, reward vaults). The pie previously showed Treasury, Team, Holdings and Escrow as separate slices.
events.backfillNote: Display-level only. The supply-reconciliation and treasury-history feeds keep their original category keys (treasury, council, holdings, team, staking, escrow), so no historical row changes and nothing needs a backfill; only how the Supply view groups them changed. Whether developer holdings circulate is not asserted by this grouping; the circulating figure is computed exactly as before.
events.uiNote: Four slices (Treasury, Team, Holdings, Escrow) merge into one Developer holdings slice. Hover or tap it for the sub-category breakdown with wallet addresses. Classification display change, not a transfer of tokens.
